import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set a clean aesthetic style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Generate a grouped violin plot to show the distribution of camera prices
# categorized by sensor type and further broken down by body type.
# The 'inner="quartile"' option displays the median and interquartile range.
# 'cut=0' ensures the violin plot does not extend beyond the actual data range.
sns.violinplot(
    data=df,
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='body_type',
    inner='quartile',
    palette='Paired', # A categorical color palette
    cut=0
)

# Apply a logarithmic scale to the y-axis (price) to better visualize distributions
# across a wide range of prices, especially if there are many lower-priced items
# and a few very expensive ones.
plt.yscale('log')

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices by Sensor Type and Body Type', fontsize=16)

# Label the x-axis
plt.xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=12)

# Label the y-axis, indicating the log scale
plt.ylabel('Price (USD) [Log Scale]', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if they are long or numerous
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Place the legend outside the plot area to prevent overlap with data points
plt.legend(title='Body Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to ensure all elements (title, labels, legend) fit without clipping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

    data=df,
    x='sensor_type',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='body_type',
    inner='quartile',
    palette='Paired', # A categorical color palette
    cut=0
)

# Apply a logarithmic scale to the y-axis (price) to better visualize distributions
# across a wide range of prices, especially if there are many lower-priced items
# and a few very expensive ones.
plt.yscale('log')

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Prices by Sensor Type and Body Type', fontsize=16)
